[[File:Bounty Hunter logo (Minigame Teleport).png|left]]
'''Bounty Hunter''', commonly abbreviated as '''BH''', is a [[player killing]] [[minigame]] located in the [[Wilderness]] at [[Daimon's Crater]]. Upon entering the crater, the player will be given another player within 5 (adjustable to 10 or 15 by speaking with the [[Emblem Trader]]) combat levels of them as a target. Besides the usual items dropped on death, players who successfully kill their target will be rewarded with Bounty Hunter points, which can be used at the Emblem Trader's [[Bounty Hunter Store]].

Bounty Hunter can be accessed via the Bounty Hunter portal in the [[Ferox Enclave]].

==Mechanics==
===Coffer===
To participate in Bounty Hunter, players are required to put minimum deposit of [[coins]] into the [[Coffer (Bounty Hunter)|Bounty Hunter coffer]]. The minimum deposit depends on the player's combat level:
{| class="wikitable"
!Combat Level
!Minimum Deposit 
|-
|32-60
|{{Coins|30,000}}
|-
|61-88
|{{Coins|50,000}}
|-
|89-110
|{{Coins|100,000}}
|-
|111-126
|{{Coins|150,000}}
|}
Upon a player's death, on top of the standard item loss to [[PvP]] death, an amount of coins are deducted from the coffer. Non-skulled players lose coins equal to their minimum deposit, while [[Skull (status)|skulled]] players only lose {{Coins|10,000}}.

===Skulls===
Bounty Hunter uses unique versions of the skull symbol that indicates how much a player is currently risking. A skull with yellow eyes indicates a player is also [[Skull (status)|skulled]].

[[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter) icon (1).png]][[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter, skulled) icon (1).png]] — Bronze skull, risking up to {{Coins|200,000}}

[[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter) icon (2).png]][[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter, skulled) icon (2).png]] — Iron skull, risking between {{Coins|200,001}} and {{Coins|800,000}}

[[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter) icon (3).png]][[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter, skulled) icon (3).png]] — Green skull, risking between {{Coins|800,001}} and {{Coins|2,000,000}}

[[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter) icon (4).png]][[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter, skulled) icon (4).png]] — Blue skull, risking between {{Coins|2,000,001}} and {{Coins|8,000,000}}

[[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter) icon (5).png]][[File:Skull (Bounty Hunter, skulled) icon (5).png]] — Red skull, risking  {{Coins|8,000,001}} or more

{{Bug|Currently, skulls do not take into account the value of untradeable items, such as degraded Barrows equipment.}}

===Fighting===
When you enter the crater, you will spawn somewhere in the arena and be given a target from amongst the other players in the minigame. While in the crater, [[teleportation]] is blocked, though [[Teleport to Target]] may be used if the player has not been in combat within the last 12 seconds. Additionally, [[protection prayers]] cannot be used, [[phoenix necklace]]s will not activate, and binding spells such as [[ice spells|ice]] and [[grasp spells]] will not stop players' movement.

Players may create bounty supply crates to bring in more supplies. These come in two variants: [[Bounty supply crate (manta ray)|manta ray crates]] and [[Bounty supply crate (anglerfish)|anglerfish crates]]. Crates are filled with eight [[blighted manta ray]]s/[[blighted anglerfish]], two [[blighted karambwan]], one [[blighted super restore(4)]], and 1,000 coins. Up to two crates may be brought inside Bounty Hunter at a time, although players may make and store these crates en masse.

[[(bh)|Equipment]] ending in the (bh) [[suffix]] can only be used in PvP minigames including Bounty Hunter, providing very strong bonuses and [[special attacks]]. These weapons and armour (most being variants of [[Ancient Warriors' equipment]]) can be obtained from the [[Bounty Hunter Store]] by either purchasing directly, or by purchasing an imbue scroll to upgrade a regular item. These items (excluding the imbued items) must be charged with {{Coins|5000000}} (armour, Vesta's spear, Zuriel's staff, Morrigan's throwing axe), {{Coins|10000000}} (Statius's warhammer, Morrigan's javelin), or {{Coins|50000000}} (Vesta's longsword) before they can be used. Upon dying in PvP, the coins used to activate the item are given to the killer, and players are left with the inactive item.

Players who do not have the level 78 Defence requirement to wear Ancient Warriors' equipment can talk to the [[Corrupted Warrior (Bounty Hunter)|Corrupted Warrior]] to convert the item to its corrupted variant and vice versa. Corrupted Ancient Warriors' equipment only requires 20 Defence, but has far lower bonuses than its uncorrupted variant.

===Earning Potential===
Earning Potential (also known as EP) can be gained by spending time inside the crater. Your EP value increases by 1% every 30 seconds you spend in the crater, capping at 100%. When unskulled, you receive 50% less EP per minute. If you have a target and are risking at least {{Coins|50000}}, your EP value will increase by twice as much, resulting in 2% EP gained per 30 seconds. The higher your EP, the higher tier [[Bounty crate]] you can receive as a drop upon defeating an opponent. Upon receiving a bounty crate, your EP is reset back to 0%. 

{{Bounty crate values|fullname=yes}}

===Bounty Hunter points===
Each target kill will earn you two Bounty Hunter points, which can be traded for rewards at the [[Bounty Hunter Store]]. In addition, bonus points are rewarded for milestone kills:
{| class="wikitable"
!Total Kill Count
!Bonus Points
|-
|Per 10th
|3
|-
|Per 50th
|5
|-
|Per 100th
|10
|-
|Per 500th
|25
|}
Besides the points earned from kills, players can earn extra points by levelling up and trading in [[esoteric emblem]]s. A tier 1 emblem will drop on your first target kill, or it can be bought from the Bounty Hunter Store for two points. [[Ironman Mode|Ironman]] players can only obtain a tier 1 emblem from the store. Each target kill will rank up your own emblem. Dying with an emblem will reduce its tier by 1. If the emblem has a tier of 1 upon death, it will be removed. If unskulled, your emblem cannot be upgraded past tier 5.

===Target Skipping & Penalties===
A player may skip up to two skulled targets within a thirty-minute window without incurring a penalty. Once a player skips their third skulled target, they will be blocked from matchmaking for thirty minutes. (You can skip unskulled targets without penalty) After the thirty minutes, the points rewarded after the first target killed will be halved and an esoteric emblem will not be dropped (if they don't already have one). If the player has an esoteric emblem in their inventory instead, it will not be upgraded.

==Official worlds==
{{#vardefine:weekly|{{#expr:floor(floor(({{#time:U}}-{{#time:U|31 December 2025 10:30:00 UTC}})/(60*60*24))/7) mod 2}}}}
Unlike most minigames, Bounty Hunter can only be played on certain [[worlds]]. As with PvP worlds, Bounty Hunter worlds are often [[PvP world#Rotation|rotated]] to provide fairer [[lag]] associated with ping/server latency to players across the world. The current active PvP world rotation is {{#switch:{{#var:weekly}}|0=[[Server#Rotation_A|Rotation A]]|1=[[Server#Rotation_B|Rotation B]]}}.{{purge|tag=sup}}<!-- #switch strings are used for automatically updating weekly rotations. 0 = rotation A; 1 = rotation B. The date listed in the string is when the rotation switches to A. --> Worlds 318 (UK) and 569 (AUS) are available on rotation A, and world 319 (US West) is available on rotation B.

==Trivia==
*Originally released in December 2007 as part of the highly controversial update that saw the removal of PvP from the Wilderness, Bounty Hunter's first incarnation was confined to a single {{RSL|Wilderness Volcano|crater}} and was intended as a substitute for Wilderness player-killing. Although the [[August 2007 Archive of RuneScape|August 2007 archive of RuneScape]] that ''Old School RuneScape''{{'}}s servers were based on predated the Bounty Hunter update, both players and the development team expressed interest in bringing it back in a revised form. It was subsequently released in 2014 as a single-world activity that existed separately from and alongside traditional Wilderness PvP. Likewise, the current version of Bounty Hunter also did not replace traditional PvP combat, instead serving as an optional minigame.
*The [[Emblem Trader]] manages the Bounty Hunter minigame, and talking to him in free-to-play reveals that he was entrusted this responsibility by his "master in [[the north]]", who is likely a [[Mahjarrat]].
